formula: y ~ gender + I(age - 12) + I((age - 12)^2) + (1 | id)
notes: Read help page (Muscatine Coronary Risk Factor Study obesity; Woolson & Clarke 1984). y = obese 0/1 (missing allowed), biennial occasions; id = child. The R code of Fitzmaurice, Laird and Ware (2011, sec. 13.4) fits a marginal logistic model by GEE, ordgee(ordered(y) ~ factor(gender) + cage + cage2 + factor(gender):cage + factor(gender):cage2, id = id, waves = occasion, corstr = 'unstructured') with cage = age - 12, then model2 without the gender interactions; its SAS code tests them by a Wald contrast and drops them too. The subject cluster of the marginal model is rendered as a random intercept (geepack ruling, m3#22); the quadratic stays in the formula only, age named once (muscatine, m3#22). occasion and baseage are alternate time axes, unused usable columns. Outside check: the book's final model replaces its first fit with the gender interactions.

formula: malform ~ dose + (1 | id)
notes: Read help page (NTP ethylene-glycol developmental-toxicity study; Price et al. 1985). id = litter, multiple fetuses per litter. malform = fetal malformation (binary), with a litter random intercept over dose. Gueorguieva and Agresti (2001, JASA 96, sec. 4) fit a correlated probit model to these data: malformation by a probit and fetal weight by a Gaussian model, each on dose, their litter intercepts correlated (not read here: the paper's copy on the author's site is gone). This row is its binary part, weight its model 2, ignored here. Outside check: stands, the probit filed as the family.

formula: weight ~ dose + (1 | id)
notes: Second response of the NTP litter data: fetal weight (continuous) over the same litter grouping, the Gaussian part of Gueorguieva and Agresti's (2001, sec. 4) correlated probit model (not read here); malformation is model 1, ignored here. Outside check: stands; the quadratic dose term the paper tests files no row.

formula: y ~ trt + time + trt:time + (1 | id)
notes: Read help page (insomnia clinical trial; Francom, Chuang-Stein & Landis 1989, Agresti 2002 Table 11.4). y = 4-level ordinal time-to-fall-asleep at baseline and 2 weeks; id = patient. Repeated cumulative-logit model with treatment-by-time interaction as the key test. medium. Outside check: stands; Agresti (2002, sec. 12.4.2, Table 12.7) fits this cumulative-logit model with a patient intercept (not read here).

formula: standardize(score) ~ 0 + (1 | judge) + (1 | wine), each index's SD fixed at 0.5 by its prior
documented_prior: a[jid] ~ dnorm(0,0.5); w[wid] ~ dnorm(0,0.5); sigma ~ dexp(1)
notes: Scores of 20 wines (a white and a red flight of 10, French and from New Jersey) by 9 judges (French and American), blind to the wines (Wines2012.Rd). McElreath's 2020 course, week 5 (homework/week05/week05_script.R), fits m1: the standardized score ~ normal(a[judge] + w[wine], sigma), a and w each normal(0, 0.5) without a hyperprior; its m2a, m2b and m3 regress the score on wine.amer, judge.amer and flight without the judge and wine indices. The fixed scales keep the grouping and are named in the formula (rugby, #15). wine.amer, judge.amer and flight are unused usable columns. Outside check: m1 replaces the reading's combination of the two models.

formula: vsae ~ I(age - 2) + I((age - 2)^2) + sicdegp + I(age - 2):sicdegp + (0 + I(age - 2) + I((age - 2)^2) | childid)
notes: West, Welch and Galecki (2007, ch. 6): socialization scores (VSAE) of autistic children at ages 2, 3, 5, 9 and 13 by their expressive-language group at age 2 (sicdegp, 3 levels); 612 rows of 158 children, 2 without vsae. The book's script (WWGbook inst/scripts/ch06.R) fits model1.fit with age.2 = age - 2, its square, sicdegp and both their interactions and a correlated random intercept and linear and quadratic slopes per child, drops the random intercept (model2.fit), tests the quadratic slope against model2a.fit, and keeps model3.fit, which drops the quadratic-by-group interaction by a likelihood-ratio test. The centering and the quadratic stay in the formula only, age named once; the contract adds a random intercept. Outside check: the book's final model replaces the recalled one.

formula: CD4 ~ I(time * (time > 0)) + (1 | id)
notes: Diggle's APTS data set: CD4 cell counts of 369 HIV seroconverters (2376 rows) over time in years since seroconversion, the banner's other columns (age, smoke, drug, partners, cesd, some centered) explanatory. Diggle's APTS lecture notes (APTS_lectures.pdf, 'A random effects model for CD4 cell counts') fit lm(CD4 ~ time), lme(CD4 ~ time, random = ~1|id) and last fit3 = lme(CD4 ~ timeplus, random = ~1|id), timeplus = time*(time > 0) holding the mean constant before seroconversion; the hinge stays in the formula only, time named once. The integer counts are count by the census rule, the lecture's Gaussian fit in family. Diggle, Heagerty, Liang and Zeger (2002) analyse these covariates on the MACS CD4 data (not read here); age, smoke, drug, partners and cesd are unused usable columns. Outside check: the lecture's final fit replaces the recalled random-slope model.

formula: eval ~ beauty + (1 | course_id)
notes: ROS Beauty (Gelman, Hill and Vehtari 2020, ch. 10; Hamermesh and Parker's teaching evaluations), 463 course evaluations. beauty.Rmd fits stan_glm(eval ~ beauty), adds female, age, minority, nonenglish and lower in fit_2 to fit_7, and fits fit_8 = stan_glm(eval ~ beauty + factor(course_id)), the course as fixed indicators. Rendered as a random intercept on course_id, a repeating cluster (ROS, m3#25), at low as fixed blocks are (mead.germination, m3#22); code 0 pools the courses taught once (306 rows). female, age, minority, nonenglish and lower are unused usable columns. The raw ProfEvaltnsBeautyPublic.csv carries a professor id (profnumber), a grouping of the same 463 rows lost with its exclusion as a duplicate. Outside check: fit_8's covariates; published_model stays no, as for the other fixed-block renderings (Traffic, appletaste).

formula: logfev1 ~ age + log(ht) + baseage + log(baseht) + (1 + age | id)
notes: Read help page (Six Cities Study, Topeka girls; Dockery et al. 1983). Long form, 300 girls, 1-12 visits; id = girl. logfev1 is log(FEV1), the raw FEV1 not in the table. FLW lung-growth linear mixed model of log FEV1 on height and age; baseht/baseage are time-invariant baseline values. medium. SPOT CHECK (Alex, 2026-10-08): the documented model uses log height, log baseline height and a random slope in age with unstructured covariance. Outside check: stands, the R code read: sec. 8.8 fits model1 (this row), model2 with a log-height slope and model3 with both slopes, without choosing between them; sec. 9.6 fits logfev1 - 2*log(ht), the same response with an offset, on age.

formula: away_score ~ 1 + (1 | away_team) + (1 | home_team)
documented_prior: intercept ~ Normal(3, 1); sd_att ~ HalfNormal(2); sd_def ~ HalfNormal(2)
notes: Code read #15: row 2 of the bivariate rugby filing, the away_score part, examples/case_studies/rugby_analytics.myst.md:240-271: log away_theta = intercept + atts[away_team] + defs[home_team], the same sum-to-zero atts and defs as the home_score part (model_index 1); prior trimmed to this part (home is in the home_score part only). home_score is the other response (ignored); year unused. Fits pass #111: the formula cell's remark moved here: the away_score part of the bivariate Poisson fit mvbind(home_score, away_score); away_team indexes attack, home_team defence; attack and defence are one team-indexed pair shared with the home_score part, each centred to sum to zero over the 6 teams; no home advantage. Fits pass #111: the formula cell's remark moved here: the away_score part of the bivariate Poisson fit mvbind(home_score, away_score); away_team indexes attack, home_team defence; attack and defence are one team-indexed pair shared with the home_score part, each centred to sum to zero over the 6 teams; no home advantage. Outside check: stands; unlike kl_dyads, the model has no match effect, so the table is not wide.

formula: conc ~ age + (age || Lot)
notes: Radioimmunoassay of IGF-I: estimated concentration (conc) by tracer age in days, 10 lots (IGF.Rd; Davidian and Giltinan 1995; Pinheiro and Bates 2000, App. A.11). Pinheiro and Bates (2000, sec. 4.2; nlme's scripts/ch04.R) fit fm2IGF.lme = lme(conc ~ age, IGF, random = pdDiag(~age)), uncorrelated intercept and age effects per Lot, diagnose it, and test the random intercept against fm3IGF.lme (random = ~ age - 1). Outside check: the book's linear model replaces the recalled four-parameter logistic, so the row is no longer nonlinear.

formula: conc ~ one-compartment oral PK model (time, dose, interval); log(Cl) ~ glyco + Creatinine + Weight, log(V) and log(Ka) constant; uncorrelated Subject effects on log(V) and log(Cl); residual SD a power of the fitted concentration
notes: NONLINEAR: Quinidine.Rd (App. A.25; Davidian and Giltinan 1995, sec. 9.3). nlme's scripts/ch08.R (Pinheiro and Bates 2000, sec. 8.2) fits fm1Quin.nlme = nlme(conc ~ quinModel(Subject, time, conc, dose, interval, lV, lKa, lCl), fixed = lV + lKa + lCl ~ 1, random = pdDiag(lV + lCl ~ 1)), adds glyco (fm2), Creatinine (fm3) and Weight (fm4) to the log clearance, then fm5 = update(fm4, weights = varPower()), compared by anova; the script comments out every fit after fm2 ('subsequent fits don't work'). Dosing rows have conc = NaN with a dose and are no observations. Outside check: Weight enters the clearance, not the volume, and fm5 is filed.

formula: conc ~ three-compartment IV infusion PK model (Time, Rate, Amt); subject-specific parameters, covariates Age and LBM
notes: NONLINEAR: Read Remifentanil.Rd (Minto et al. 1997; P&B 2000 as source). Page shows only plots, no model; the Minto model uses age and lean body mass. ID is a numeric copy of Subject and BSA a derived column; LBM also derived but kept as the documented covariate. First rows: first row of each patient has conc = NaN. RULE GAP: nonlinear PK model with time-varying infusion input; derived columns BSA and LBM. Spot check (Alex): model class named; dosing rows carry no conc and are not observations. Outside check: stands; Minto et al. (1997) fit three-compartment models with Age and LBM covariates (not read here).

formula: conc ~ biexponential(Time; Formulation effect; random effects on Subject)
notes: NONLINEAR: Tetracycline1.Rd names no model (Pinheiro and Bates 2000 as source, whose scripts fit none): a crossover pharmacokinetic study, 5 subjects each under two formulations (tetrachel, tetracyn), concentration over Time. A reader would fit a compartmental concentration-time model, nonlinear in its parameters; the biexponential is the reading's choice. conc is the help's pharmacokinetic measurement, so the response is not inferred. Outside check: published_model no, as no source fits a model.

formula: Surv(time, cens) ~ treat + (1 | pair)
notes: Matched-pairs leukemia remission trial, 21 pairs of two patients, one given 6-MP and one the control. MASS's scripts/ch13.R fits survreg(Surv(time, cens) ~ factor(pair) + treat, gehan, dist = 'exponential') and coxph(Surv(time, cens) ~ treat + factor(pair), gehan), the pair a fixed block; rendered with a random pair intercept at low (mead.germination, m3#22), published_model no as for Traffic. Survival: time continuous, cens in ignore, Surv() in the formula (catheter, m3#24); the exponential family is outside Family. Outside check: Surv() in the formula, published_model no.

formula: result ~ gender + pan_day + age + demo_group + patient_class + (1 | clinic_name) + (1 | subject_id)
notes: RESPONSE INFERRED: deidentified SARS-CoV-2 PCR testing at CHOP in 2020 (Obstfeld; medicaldata). Page documents the data but names no model or response. Chose result (test result positive/negative/invalid, three levels so filed categorical) as the outcome the data were collected to study, with clinic_name (88 clinics/wards) and subject_id crossed as grouping factors and gender, pan_day (day of pandemic), age, demo_group and patient_class as predictors: 1744 of 12344 subjects are tested more than once, 244 of them with differing results, and 734 in two or more clinics. The fake first and last names (identifiers), test_id, ct_result (cycle-threshold, an alternate lab response), drive_thru_ind, orderset, payor_group and the two turnaround times col_rec_tat and rec_ver_tat in ignore. Outside check: subject_id joins the grouping.

formula: Goals ~ Gender + Grade + Age + Race + `Urban/Rural` + (1 | School)
notes: DASL PopularKids (Chase & Dummer 1992); students of grades 4-6 in 9 schools report their most important goal (Goals: Grades/Sports/Popular), OpenML's default target; School the clustering unit. Grades/Sports/Looks/Money are the four-factor rankings (alternate outcomes), ignored. No model documented; formula is the natural random-intercept over School. Retained School assumes exchangeable sampling from a larger population of schools; this remains unverified. Outside check: the response is documented, not inferred.

formula: I(readmitted == "<30") ~ discharge_home + race + admission_source + specialty_group + age_group + diag_1_group + time_in_hospital + HbA1c_group + discharge_home:race + discharge_home:specialty_group + discharge_home:diag_1_group + discharge_home:time_in_hospital + specialty_group:time_in_hospital + specialty_group:age_group + diag_1_group:time_in_hospital + diag_1_group:HbA1c_group + (1|patient_nbr)
notes: Diabetes 130-US hospitals (Strack et al. 2014): 101766 encounters, patient_nbr repeats (up to 40 encounters per patient) so it is a genuine within-patient cluster. readmitted (NO/<30/>30) the documented target. Strack et al. de-duplicate to one encounter per patient and fit logistic regression (not mixed), so confidence low. encounter_id ignored; Hand sample #13 (O/low blind re-read): covariates and interactions are the final model of Strack et al. 2014 (sections 2.3-3, Tables 4-5): readmission within 30 days on the first encounter per patient, logistic, no random effects, so the patient intercept stays proposed. Recodes in the formula: discharge_home from discharge_disposition_id (home or other), admission_source from admission_source_id (emergency, referral, other), specialty_group from medical_specialty, age_group from age ([0,30), [30,60), [60,100)), diag_1_group the ICD-9 groups of diag_1, HbA1c_group from A1Cresult and change (no test, normal, high and changed, high and unchanged). RULE GAP: derived interaction; diag_1_group:HbA1c_group is in the formula only, diag_1:A1Cresult not being its encoding. Outside check: the formula keeps the recodes and the fields their raw columns, by the #162 ruling (a benchmark task's recode stays in the formula only).

formula: Stay_Days ~ Hospital_type + Hospital_region + Hospital_city + Available_Extra_Rooms_in_Hospital + Department + Ward_Type + Ward_Facility + Bed_Grade + Type_of_Admission + Illness_Severity + Patient_Visitors + Age + Admission_Deposit + City_Code_Patient + (1|Hospital) + (1|patientid)
notes: Analytics-Vidhya healthcare hackathon (OpenML COVID-19-Hospitals-Treatment-Plan): predict length-of-stay class (Stay_Days, 11 ordered bins, filed categorical as >10 levels) per admission; Hospital (32) the clustering unit, patients repeat within. No published mixed model; formula is the natural random-intercept over Hospital. case_id ignored. Hand sample #13 (O/low blind re-read): patientid added, crossed with Hospital: patients recur across hospitals (92017 patients, 3.5 admissions each, 75% in more than one hospital); City_Code_Patient added beside Hospital_city, the two measure different locations; a city nested in a region stays in the predictor inventory, redundant contrasts being a fitting issue. Outside check: the 11 ordered bins stay categorical, past the merge's cap of ten levels on an ordinal response.

formula: diagnostic ~ smoke + drink + background_father + background_mother + age + pesticide + gender + skin_cancer_history + cancer_history + has_piped_water + has_sewage_system + fitspatrick + region + diameter_1 + diameter_2 + itch + grew + hurt + changed + bleed + elevation + (1|patient_id)
notes: PAD-UFES-20 skin-lesion dataset (Pacheco et al. 2020): 2298 images, 1373 patients (up to 10 images/lesions per patient); diagnostic (6 lesion types) the documented classification target, patient_id the clustering unit. No mixed model; formula is the natural random-intercept over patient_id. img_id/biopsed ignored. Hand sample #13 (O/low blind re-read) added lesion_id for the authors' patient > lesion > image hierarchy (arXiv 2007.00478). Outside check: lesion_id leaves the grouping: 250 lesion ids recur across patients, and each of the 1891 patient:lesion pairs holds one diagnosis (one label per group).

formula: y ~ gender + age + majority_first + (1 | culture)
notes: Social-learning experiment of van Leeuwen et al. (2018, Nature Communications 9): children of 8 sites (culture) choose among three options after demonstrations; Boxes.Rd defines y (1 the unchosen, 2 the majority, 3 the minority option), gender, age, majority_first and culture. The book (R code 16.7-16.8, m16.2) fits a mixture of five choice strategies without culture effects; the paper's regressions are not read here. The culture intercept is a proposal. Outside check: the response is documented; the formula stays proposed.

formula: social_learning ~ log(research_effort) + log(body) + log(brain) + (1 | genus)
notes: McElreath's Primates301: 301 primate species, one row each. The Rd example mP301GP (man/Primates301.Rd) fits social_learning ~ poisson, log lambda = a + g[spp_id] + b_ef*log(research_effort) + b_body*log(body) + b_eq*log(brain), g a Gaussian process over species with the L2 covariance of phylogenetic distance (Primates301_distance_matrix), on the 150 complete species; the book's ch. 14 phylogenetic regression (m14.9-m14.11) models brain size and is model 2. The species process is observation-level, and no source fits genus; genus repeats (68 genera) and groups by the #24 rule, its intercept a proposal. group_size and the life-history columns are not in the model. Outside check: published_model no, the Gaussian process in notes.
